page.title: Terminal Workspace
page.purpose: Run and steer many terminal sessions from one surface: start a first session in seconds, keep the active session's output at the visual center, switch sessions at a glance, and never be lied to about connection or recovery state.

priorities.statement: A first-time visitor reaches a live shell within seconds of arriving.
The active session's output owns the visual center at all times; chrome stays ambient.
Session identity and switching are one glance away, in every display mode.
Connection and recovery truth is always visible — the console never silently lies about liveness.
Voice and AI input are discoverable without ever competing with the terminal.

states.description: Store hydration / initial health check before the workspace is interactive.
No sessions yet: tagline plus the new-terminal affordance as the one path forward.
One or more live sessions; active pane output streaming.
The new-terminal launcher dialog is open (shortcuts, custom command, backend options).
Async session recovery in progress after reload; honestly bannered while usable.
API unreachable: connection banner with retry, auto-clearing when health returns.
Mic engaged (recording/listening/transcribing) with visible state on the mic control.

regions.purpose: Stable hydrated shell marker used by capture and workflow consumers before inspecting workspace controls.

elements.description: Primary affordance to start a session; present in empty state and ambient chrome.
New-terminal launcher: default shortcuts, custom command, backend/timeout options.
xterm.js pane host — no adequate native ARIA role; x- custom role by design (spike: exercises the escape hatch).
Session tabs with selected state (tabs display mode).
Command input in the mobile toolbar; queued/failed send status alongside.
Voice input control with visible state machine (idle/recording/listening/transcribing) and auto-stop ring.
AI command palette entry in the ambient toolbar.
API-unreachable banner with retry; polls and auto-clears.

claims.statement: The empty workspace presents the new-terminal affordance immediately; there is no dead-end arrival.
With no sessions, starting one is the single dominant action; nothing competes.
The new-terminal launcher opens as an announced dialog, keyboard-dismissable.
A terminal surface is perceivable and central whenever sessions exist — including during recovery and voice capture.
In tabs mode, sessions are exposed as a tablist with the active tab selected.
On mobile, the command composer is perceivable alongside the terminal without hunting.
The composer and its send affordance are fully keyboard operable.
While sessions recover after a reload, a status banner discloses it; recovery is never silent.
When the API is unreachable, a status banner says so and offers retry; it clears itself when health returns.
Voice input is discoverable from the primary surface without opening any menu.
A first-time visitor reaches a live shell in at most three interactions from the empty state.
Toolbars, banners, and the audio bar never occlude the active terminal's most recent output line.
Composer drafts survive reloads and session switches; typed input is never lost.
Panes cycle with Ctrl+Tab / Ctrl+Shift+Tab and jump with Ctrl+1–9; heavy users never need the pointer to switch sessions.
App chrome tints to the active terminal's palette, so the console feels of-a-piece with the session rather than framing it.
claims.rationale: The ambient-chrome identity claim; becomes checkable with the P2 saliency/palette tier.

claims.statement: In every display mode, the active pane's output dominates attention; chrome and siblings recede.
claims.rationale: Priority 2 as a saliency claim (P2 importance ranking).

new-terminal.note: Empty-state instance; ambient instances are toolbar-new / tab-bar-new / workspace-sidebar-new.

x-display-modes.note: Display mode is a user-selectable layout dimension ORTHOGONAL to the lifecycle states above (a mode x state matrix). scenario-experience-spec/v1 has no first-class axis for this, so mode-scoped claims carry x-display-mode; open-world semantics absorb it. SPIKE LEARNING: if this recurs across scenarios, promote a generalized 'dimensions' axis in a schema minor version rather than overloading states.

x-spike.verdict-source: Operator judgment: web-console UX is exceptional — machine claims are expected to PASS; any failure is either a genuine edge (e.g. connection banner not exposed as status) or a spec mis-assumption to fix. Mirror image of the business-health calibration.
vocabulary-stress-notes: Single route '/': the routes-based page model held, but only because overlays could be modeled as states.
x-terminal custom role: the ARIA registry has no terminal role; the x- escape hatch was required, not optional.
No DESIGN.md: state list was authored from observed behavior instead of a seeded contract; parser must not hard-require the seed.
Display modes needed x- scoping on claims (see x-display-modes).
